overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #1007 asks: what is the smallest number of edges in a 4-dimensional graph? The graph dimension dim(G) is the minimum n such that G can be embedded as a unit distance graph in ℝⁿ (all edges have Euclidean length exactly 1). Paul Erdős posed this question in the context of unit distance geometry, an area he contributed to substantially. The answer — 9 edges, uniquely achieved by K_{3,3} — was proved by House (2013) using geometric case analysis. The 5-dimensional analogue (minimum 15 edges) was settled by Chaffee and Noble (2016). This OQ-05 entry is an axiom elimination analysis: one of four axioms in the parent formalization (hasUnitEmbedding_exists) can be proved constructively via scaled standard basis vectors. A notable finding: the original axiom statement contained a subtle logical error — it asserts every finite graph has a unit distance embedding, but this fails for graphs with self-loops (where dist(v,v) = 0 ≠ 1). The corrected theorem adds irreflexivity, recovering the intended mathematical content.
overview.problemStatement:
**OQ-05**: Can the axioms in the Erdős #1007 formalization be proved?

**Answer**: One of four axioms (`hasUnitEmbedding_exists`) is proved via scaled standard basis vectors. The remaining three encode deep results from House (2013) and Chaffee-Noble (2016).
overview.proofStrategy: For `hasUnitEmbedding_exists`: map vertex v to (1/√2)·e_{φ(v)} in ℝ^|V|, where φ : V ≃ Fin |V|. All distinct pairs are at distance exactly 1.
keyInsights: Axiom bug discovery: the original hasUnitEmbedding_exists axiom is false for graphs with self-loops, since any unit distance embedding must satisfy dist(f(v), f(v)) = 0 ≠ 1; the corrected theorem requires ∀ v, ¬adj v v
Scaled basis construction: map vertex v to (1/√2)·e_{φ(v)} in ℝ^|V|; for distinct u, v, the vectors are at orthogonal positions, so ‖f(u)−f(v)‖² = (1/√2)² + (1/√2)² = 1 exactly
The private lemma scaled_basis_sq_dist isolates the key calculation: Σ_k (δ_{ik}/√2 − δ_{jk}/√2)² = 1 for i ≠ j; this algebraic fact is the sole non-trivial step

min_edges_dimension_4 is the real challenge: proving every graph with dim = 4 has ≥9 edges requires showing all graphs with ≤8 edges embed in ℝ³ — a geometric case analysis not yet formalizable without specialized infrastructure
The K_{3,3} uniqueness (k33_unique_minimum) and 5-dimensional analogue (Chaffee-Noble 2016: ≥15 edges for dim = 5) remain as axioms, correctly documented with their literature sources
overview.text: Axiom elimination analysis for Erdős #1007 graph dimension formalization. Proves hasUnitEmbedding_exists (unit distance embedding existence) via scaled basis vectors, reducing from 4 to 3 axioms.

sections.title: Helper Lemma: Squared Distance Calculation
sections.summary: Private lemma scaled_basis_sq_dist proves that scaled standard basis vectors at distinct indices i ≠ j in Fin n are at squared Euclidean distance exactly 1. Uses Finset.add_sum_erase to extract the two non-zero summands.

sections.title: Main Theorem: Unit Embedding via Scaled Basis Vectors
sections.summary: Theorem hasUnitEmbedding_exists_irr: every finite graph with irreflexive adjacency admits a unit distance embedding in ℝ^|V|. Constructs the embedding using Fintype.equivFin and the scaled basis, applying the helper lemma and Real.sqrt_one.
sections.mathContext: $f(v)_k = \delta_{\varphi(v),k} / \sqrt{2}$; irreflexivity ensures $u \neq v$, so $\varphi(u) \neq \varphi(v)$ and the helper applies

sections.title: Corollary: Complete Bipartite Graphs Have Unit Embeddings
sections.summary: Proves completeBipartiteAdj is irreflexive (by cases on Fin m ⊕ Fin n), then applies the main theorem to conclude K_{m,n} always has a unit distance embedding of some dimension.
sections.mathContext: $\neg\,\text{completeBipartiteAdj}\, v\, v$ for all $v \in \text{Fin}\, m \oplus \text{Fin}\, n \Rightarrow \exists d,\; \text{hasUnitEmbedding}(K_{m,n}, d)$

sections.title: Remaining Deep Axioms: Literature Classification
sections.summary: Documents the three remaining axioms: min_edges_dimension_4 (House 2013: dim-4 graphs need ≥9 edges), k33_unique_minimum (K_{3,3} is the unique minimizer), and min_edges_dimension_5 (Chaffee-Noble 2016: dim-5 graphs need ≥15 edges). Each requires geometric rigidity analysis beyond current Lean formalization infrastructure.

conclusion.summary: Proved hasUnitEmbedding_exists_irr via the scaled standard basis construction, reducing the effective axiom count from 4 to 3. Also corrected a logical error in the original axiom (false for self-loops), proved K_{m,n}'s irreflexivity and unit embedding existence as corollaries, and documented the three deep remaining axioms with their literature sources.
conclusion.implications: The constructive proof demonstrates a clean and general technique: every finite loopless graph embeds as a unit distance graph in ℝ^|V| via scaled standard basis vectors. This is a folklore result that was previously only axiomatized in the formalization. The bug discovery illustrates an important aspect of formal proof: axioms can encode mathematically false statements, and Lean's type system does not catch logical falsity — only type errors. The three remaining axioms (House 2013, Chaffee-Noble 2016) represent genuine research-level results whose Lean formalization would require new combinatorial geometry infrastructure.
openQuestions: Can min_edges_dimension_4 be approached computationally? A full enumeration of graphs with ≤8 edges (finitely many, up to isomorphism) and a dimension-checking procedure could give a verified computational proof
Is there a simpler proof of K_{3,3} uniqueness (k33_unique_minimum) that avoids full graph classification — perhaps via a direct rigidity argument for the K_{3,3} structure?
What is the minimum number of edges for a 6-dimensional graph? Chaffee-Noble's methods may extend; this is an open case of Erdős's broader problem hierarchy
Can the scaled basis construction be generalized? The construction embeds every loopless graph but uses |V| dimensions; a tighter embedding might use fewer dimensions for sparse graphs
